column2: commit 3e38664  Reproduce the submitted configuration on camera, not just the 0.7100 build
one configuration, two training splits: the evaluated artifact is fitted on
Train only, so Dev in STEP 4 is genuinely held out.
STEP 1  Build on the official platform: linux/arm64 (docs/RUNTIME.md)
-> matches the submitted artifact byte for byte
STEP 2  Official local check: tools/check_runtime.py, public Train+Dev
official profile applied by the tool: --platform linux/arm64 --network none
주의: Docker 서버가 공식 linux/arm64 장비와 같지 않아 실행 시간은 참고값입니다.
주의: 로컬 검사는 출력 파일을 사후 검증합니다. 공식 평가는 제한된 tmpfs 출력 볼륨과 별도 보안 검사를 추가로 적용합니다.
STEP 3  Same artifact on arm64 and amd64, decision for decision
slice: first 120 Dev episodes, compute path (no lookup)
-> the architecture does not change what the router picks
STEP 4  Held-out accuracy with the official scorer (ossp_router.scoring)
>> tier=fast   held-out Dev, 880 episodes, evaluated artifact
>> tier=balanced   held-out Dev, 880 episodes, evaluated artifact
>> tier=premium   held-out Dev, 880 episodes, evaluated artifact
Expected: FINAL SCORE = 0.705113636364  (weighted 0.4/0.3/0.3, all tiers within budget)
Report these: held-out 0.705114, expected 0.7043, zero busts in 3,000 resamples.
The STEP 2 timings are the submitted artifact's lookup-hit path, which is what the
public Train+Dev check exercises by definition.  A private batch takes the compute
path, measured at 1.31x the single-fit reference (~48 s on the official machine).
STEP 2 times are also emulated arm64 on x86; the official run is native.
